thread.title: Alibaba Earnings: After Doubling, Could Stock Still Be Cheap?

author: Avi Salzman
title: Alibaba Earnings: After Doubling, Could Stock Still Be Cheap?
text:
Tech giants Facebook (FB), Amazon.com (AMZN), Apple (AAPL) and Microsoft (MSFT) will report earnings today and tomorrow. But let's not forget Chinese tech giant, Alibaba (BABA), which is scheduled to report earnings on Thursday .
 The stock has been riding a bullish wave, and has more than doubled in just the past year. But Raymond James analyst Aaron Kessler thinks the company's valuation still underestimates its growth potential. The shares are trading at about 28 times core commerce earnings expectations, well below Alibaba's expected 2018 commerce growth rate of 40%, he says.
Alibaba has a similar mix of businesses to Amazon.com (AMZN), with a core focus on retail sales, and growing interests in cloud computing, and digital media and entertainment. But Alibaba's stock doesn't fetch the same multiple as Amazon, which trades for about 300 times this year's earnings expectations.
Alibaba is certainly growing its customer base, but it's also gotten better at turning browsers into buyers, by using technology to customize recommendations. "We believe Alibaba continues to benefit from improved real-time personalization, which is driving improved click through rates and conversion and driving improved take rates," Kessler wrote.
Alibaba stock rose 2.3% in midday trading Wednesday to $204.34. Kessler has a Strong Buy rating with a $220 price target.
